title: Career cities with Ledger, Part 10: Africa, in under 2 minutes
summary: Hoang's request: Africa, one industry per stop across eight countries, jobs at each stop, real logos in the city scene (Lagos has three or more).

caption:
Career cities with Ledger, Part 10, crosses Africa in nine stops, and each stop shows one industry that city is a hub for, with a sourced fact and the jobs you could have there

So you will meet Tangier for car making, Ismailia for the Suez Canal, Lagos for fintech, Addis Ababa for aviation, Nairobi for mobile money, Kigali for coffee, Gaborone for diamonds, Johannesburg for stock trading, and Durban for port logistics

Save the map for later, because Part 11 starts the career series with finance careers

logos.why: Lagos-headquartered per https://techpoint.africa/guide/best-fintech-companies-in-nigeria/ (opened); OPay is a fourth option from the same page
HQ at Bole, Addis Ababa per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian_Airlines (opened); single brand
NOT VERIFIED: Nairobi base not confirmed in an opened source; KCB and Equity Bank also candidates, verify before use
Located in Sandton, Johannesburg per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg_Stock_Exchange (opened); only one brand verified, add listed companies after verification

sources.claim: Tangier: Morocco produced about 394,000 vehicles for Renault Group in 2025 at Tangier and Casablanca (Somaca), exported 82 percent; Tangier plant employs about 6,000 (Morocco World News, Jun 2026). Note: 394,000 covers both plants
Tangier: Tanger Med 11,106,164 TEU in 2025, 526,862 vehicles (port press release; PDF text not readable, figure from search summary)
Ismailia: Suez Canal revenue USD 4.67 billion (EGP 230.22 billion) in FY2025/26, up 23 percent, per SCA chair on 28 Jun 2026 (Egyptian Streets, 30 Jun 2026)
Ismailia as Suez Canal Authority base: not confirmed in any opened source
Lagos: Paystack, Interswitch, Moniepoint, OPay listed as Lagos-headquartered; Stripe acquired Paystack for USD 200 million in 2020 (Techpoint Africa)
Addis Ababa: Ethiopian Airlines hub and HQ at Bole in Addis Ababa; 17.1 million passengers FY2024 (Wikipedia, single source)
Nairobi: Safaricom M-PESA revenue grew 13.4 percent to KES 182.7 billion, year ended 31 Mar 2026 (Techweez, 7 May 2026)
Nairobi logos: Safaricom, KCB, Equity headquartered in Nairobi (not yet opened, to verify)
Kigali: Rwanda exported 23,860 t of green coffee worth over USD 148.6 million in 2025, up from 17,142 t and USD 89.8 million in 2024 (NAEB)

Gaborone: Debswana cut output 27 percent to 17.93 million carats in 2024; 50-50 joint venture of Botswana government and De Beers (Kitco/Reuters, 6 Jun 2025). Gaborone HQ not confirmed in an opened source
Johannesburg: JSE market cap R24.22 trillion with 431 listed companies, Jan 2026; located in Sandton, Johannesburg (Wikipedia JSE Limited)
Durban: port handles up to 31.4 million tons of cargo each year, undated; about 4.5 million TEU in 2019 (Wikipedia, single source)
Ethiopia coffee earned a record USD 3 billion in FY2025/26 (reserve fact for Addis Ababa, no city named)

openQuestions: Ending line: 'Part 11: finance careers' follows the series plan (Part 11 = first career episode, finance). Confirm that the series plan and slot hold; if Part 11 changes, edit beat 'next part' and the caption.
Word count is below 250-285 for the same cap reason as Part 9 (Part 5 ran 242 words in 110.9 s).

Two South Africa stops (Johannesburg, Durban); Durban rests on one undated Wikipedia figure. For more country variety replace Durban with Accra (cocoa), Abidjan (cocoa), Antananarivo (vanilla) or Dakar once a figure is opened. I could not open a source for these.

Weak: Gaborone HQ of Debswana and Ismailia as Suez Canal Authority base are not confirmed by opened sources; Addis Ababa airline figure is single-source Wikipedia (FY2024); Nairobi logos (Safaricom, KCB, Equity) are unverified; Lagos is the only stop with 3+ verified logos (Paystack, Interswitch, Moniepoint, OPay); Flutterwave is San Francisco-headquartered per Techpoint so it is excluded.

Politically sensitive: the Suez Canal stop gives only the revenue figure and says nothing about the Red Sea disruption; Ethiopia and Egypt are both shown with neutral facts. Tanger Med port figures were not opened, so the voiced Renault figure is Morocco-wide (Tangier plus Casablanca) and the line says so.
Jobs lines are example roles in the industry, not sourced vacancies; they sit on screen as chips, not in the voice.

Sweep 18 Nov 2026 (rule from Hoang's Part 6 and 7 notes: open on the region's main finance hub; big business, commodity and energy hubs before niche or creative picks): Johannesburg (stock trading) is stop 8 of 9; proposal: open on Johannesburg for finance, and add an oil and gas stop (for example Luanda or Port Harcourt) in place of a niche pick; Gaborone diamonds already fits
